# Jayrun 0.3.2 — native Windows memory pressure and history paths

Jayrun can now admit work and sample `Engine.pressure` on Windows using the
system's physical memory and the current process working set. This fixes an
`AttributeError` from the Unix memory fallback. Configured CPU memory limits
use the existing admission thresholds, so queued work can resume when memory
pressure subsides.

On Windows, `Database()` now uses `LOCALAPPDATA` even when the process has
no home directory. It uses the user profile's `AppData/Local` directory as
the fallback when `LOCALAPPDATA` is absent.

The fixes use the Python standard library. Existing graphs, settings and
history files work with this patch release.
